posts.name: PlatinumWarlock
posts.cooked:
For what it's worth, here's my 2 cents:

I would love to be a playtester.  My group loves playtesting new mechanics and new games--I'm a game designer with my own company, so they get to test out new stuff pretty often.  Right now, though, I could not justify spending money to become a playtester.  Money's a bit tight around our house, so dropping $40 wasn't an option on our end.

I love the conjecture and roundabout discussions.  I like the little hints that get dropped here and there, but they're often so obscure that it takes tons of work and cross-thread investigation to piece together the truth.

It's obvious that the Greater Than Guys are up to their eyeballs already, between prepping Vengeance, GSF, and their convention circuit.  Any post that they make takes away from their work on those items.  The forum-goers, by and large, are people who already love the game and support it vehemently.  Most, if not all, of us likely own a copy of SotM, if not several expansions.  We're people who are excited enough about SotM to discuss it, seek out more information, and even compile tons of data about it.

Why not allow playtesters to give a general overview of the characters currently being playtested?  I'm not asking for access to the playtest documents or even detailed mechanics.  If word of mouth is the best kind of free marketing, why not let the people most excited about the game spread the word? 

I understand the ins-and-outs of NDA and the like, but it'd be nice to see some concrete info coming out, even at this relatively early stage.

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
It would be interesting if we had some kind of opportunity to give you our assessment of the characters. That would be really hard, though, and >G would have to put some specific limitations on what could and couldn't be shared, which would make it even more challenging...

The playtesters don't get the character background info - we just get the card names and rules text. We don't even have art or flavor text to give us insight into the hero (other than a sketch of the hero on their character card. We might be able to talk about how each hero plays, but even that is hard to do without getting into the mechanics.

(This is best demonstrated by our playtesting of Unity, for those who haven't heard the story. A (not-insignificant) number of playtesters just didn't like her, didn't understand her, and didn't think she was a hero they would enjoy playing. We had these weird cards like Stealth Bot that took damage for others - shouldn't a stealthy bot actually just prevent its own damage? This didn't make a lot of sense. But we were missing that Unity is a Freedom Five fan, that her five key bots represented the members of the F5 (at the time). We were missing her voice from the flavor text. We were missing a lot. When we saw the proofs of those cards, many playtesters reversed their opinion of her - all those details we were missing completely changed our views.)

To answer the question, no you can't play using new Vengeful Five rules without using the V5, as it is their villain mechanic.
